## Source: amazon-inspector (5dcafa44d321e5c6169bbdd949fa1d421e5039bc53d017c00d3e5411f33db5ec)
The sole module shipped in both the sdist and the wheel, main.py, consists entirely of `exec(zlib.decompress(base64.b85decode('...')))` at the top level. The package exposes this module as `py_modules=['main']` and wires it as the `psbool` console_script, so the opaque, compressed-and-encoded blob is decoded and executed unconditionally the first time the module is imported or the CLI is invoked. There is no source, documentation, or API surface — the entire implementation is a single encoded payload, deliberately concealing its behavior from anyone inspecting the package before it runs. A boolean-logic utility has no legitimate reason to ship its implementation as an opaque exec-of-decoded-bytes blob; this is the canonical obfuscated-payload import-time execution shape and causes an arbitrary author-controlled program to run on the installer's machine.

## Source: kam193 (119ef283a7038fe02a4d309ce942bcce3a37a70ef5468749ae4f4e378d971e9d)
During import, obfuscated code exfiltrates photos and documents to a Telegram bot. It targets Android devices.
